text: BPAL (Bulk Procurement and Logistic Management System) is an integrated software and hardware system developed by CDCorp. It is designed to automate and manage the raw material supply chain for industries such as pulp, paper, bioenergy, and recycling. BPAL connects administrative software with physical hardware (like truck scales, gate readers, and dumpers) to create a contactless, automated workflow for receiving bulk materials. Its main goals are to reduce operational costs, eliminate human error, ensure worker safety, and provide real-time business intelligence. whats new ? you can check the whats new tab and see what are the new feture included.

MENU ITEM DESCRIPTIONS & USAGE 1. OPTION: Logout - Location: File > Logout - Function: Terminates the current user's session within the application. - Behavior: Returns the user to the login screen. It does not close the application window, only the active session. - Use Case: Use this when you are finished working but want to leave the application open for another user to log in. 2. OPTION: Security Lockout - Location: File > Security Lockout - Function: Locks the application interface instantly. - Behavior: Hides the current screen contents and requires a password to resume. - Use Case: Use this when stepping away from your desk (e. g. , for lunch or a break) to prevent unauthorized access without fully logging out. 3. OPTION: User Properties - Location: File > User Properties - Function: Opens the configuration window for the currently logged-in user. - Behavior: Displays a dialog box containing user details (permissions, username, preferences). - Use Case: Use this to view account details or modify specific user settings. 4. OPTION: Log Files > - Location: File > Log Files - Visual Indicator: Contains a right-facing arrow (>), indicating a sub-menu. - Function: Accesses the system's history and error tracking logs. - Behavior: Hovering over this item will reveal a secondary list of specific log types. - Use Case: Used for troubleshooting errors or auditing system history. 5. OPTION: Exit F12 - Location: File > Exit F12 - Shortcut Key: F12 - Function: Closes the BPAL Administration application completely. - Behavior: Terminates the software. - Use Case: Use this when you are completely done with the application and wish to close it on your computer. # Product Notebook Interface - Detailed Guide ## Overview The Product Notebook is a data entry and management interface used to create, view, and edit product information in the BPAL system. This document explains the field types, functionality, and user interactions available in the notebook. --- ## Field Types and Visual Indicators ### Open Fields (White Background) Fields with a white or light background are available for data entry. Users can click on these fields and input or modify information. These fields are editable and can receive user input. **Example:** The "Code" field, description fields, and the "Type" field in the product notebook are typically open fields ready for user input. ### Closed Fields (Gray Background) Fields with a gray background are locked and cannot be edited. These fields are read-only and display information that is either system-generated, auto-populated, or intentionally restricted from user modification. Users cannot enter or change data in closed fields. **Example:** Fields that display calculated values, status fields, or fields managed by system rules may appear grayed out. --- ## Field Icons and Their Meanings ### Magnifying Glass Icon (Lookup Table Field) The magnifying glass icon indicates that the field has a lookup table associated with it. This is standard functionality in BPAL for fields with this icon. **Functionality:** - Clicking on the magnifying glass icon opens a lookup dialog or dropdown menu - The lookup table contains a predefined list of valid values for that field - Users can select an appropriate value from the list instead of typing it manually - Lookup fields ensure data consistency and prevent invalid entries - The lookup helps users find and select the correct code or value quickly **Example:** The "Type" field in the product notebook has a magnifying glass icon, allowing users to browse and select from available product types like "BROWNGRADE". ### Information Icon (Circular "i" Icon) Located to the right of the magnifying glass icon, this circular icon with the letter "i" provides quick access to additional information related to the code field.

Helps users understand what each code represents without leaving the notebook - Provides context-sensitive help and reference information **Example:** Clicking the "i" icon next to a product type code would display the full definition, properties, and other details about that product type. --- ## Tabs and Sections The Product Notebook includes multiple tabs for organizing different types of information: ### Available Tabs - **Properties:** Contains basic product information such as code, description, category, and type - **Scaling:** Manages size, weight, or dimension scaling parameters - **Test:** Contains testing criteria and quality assurance information - **Other:** Miscellaneous additional product information and properties - **Delivery Point:** Information related to delivery locations and logistics - **Product Group:** Classification and grouping information for the product - **Unit Of Measure:** Definition of measurement units used for the product - **Audit:** Historical tracking and audit trail information about product changes Each tab organizes related fields logically, allowing users to navigate between different categories of product information. --- ## Field Components - This allows the user to choose between saving changes or discarding them. - **Behavior - If No Changes Were Made:** If no data has been changed in the notebook, pressing the Cancel button or the X in the top right corner will close the notebook immediately without any user confirmation prompt. - **Use When:** You want to exit the notebook. If you have made changes, you will be prompted to save or discard them. If you haven't made changes, the notebook closes immediately.

" - User options: - **Save:** Saves all changes and closes the notebook - **Don't Save:** Discards all changes and closes the notebook - **Cancel:** Returns to the notebook to continue editing **Scenario 2: User Made No Changes and Presses Cancel or X** - The notebook detects that no data has been modified - The notebook closes immediately without any confirmation prompt - No dialog appears - the action is instantaneous ### X Button in Top Right Corner The X button in the top right corner of the notebook window behaves identically to the Cancel button: - If changes were made, it triggers the confirmation dialog - If no changes were made, it closes the notebook immediately ### Why This Matters This change detection feature protects users from accidentally losing work. By prompting for confirmation only when changes exist, it also prevents unnecessary dialogs when simply reviewing data without making edits.

Open the Product Notebook 2. Navigate to the appropriate tab (Properties, Scaling, Test, etc. ) 3. Locate the open (white background) field you want to edit 4. Click on the field and enter or modify the data 5. If the field has a magnifying glass icon, click it to select from a lookup table 6. Click **Apply** to save and continue editing, or **OK** to save and close ### To View Additional Details About a Selection 1. Click the magnifying glass icon to open the lookup table 2. Select the desired value 3. Click the circular "i" icon next to the field 4. Review the information popup that appears 5. Close the popup and proceed with your work ### To Discard Changes 1. Click the **Cancel** button 2. All unsaved changes will be discarded 3. The notebook will close without modifying the database --- ## Best Practices 1. **Use Lookup Fields:** Always use the magnifying glass icon for fields that have it - this ensures you select valid values 2.

ODBC Methodology Event Tracking & Alert System: The Data Storage Phase Version 2. 0 ​​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​​ CHAPTER 1 – INTRODUCTION 1. 1 Overview The Event Tracking System (Phase 1) is a comprehensive database-driven solution designed to capture and store system events across the entire BPAL application and services. Built with scalability and flexibility in mind, this system provides a centralized repository for all application events, establishing the foundation for future notification capabilities. “Note: This document covers Phase 1 (Data Storage). Phase 2 (Real-Time Notification System) will be planned separately once the data layer is stable. ” 1. 2 Purpose In modern distributed systems, tracking events across multiple applications, services, and platforms presents significant challenges. Phase 1 addresses these challenges by providing: Capability Description Centralized Event Logging A single source of truth for all system events across BPAL Comprehensive Audit Trail Complete history of all events with timestamps and context Flexible Event Data Storage Support for structured and unstructured event data Event Classification Categorization framework for different event types and priorities Multi-Language Support Bilingual descriptions (English/French) User Event Subscription Users can subscribe to specific event configurations with per-user notification preferences and data filters Notification Signaling Lightweight kick records enable immediate notification service activation when events are logged, without impacting event insertion performance Out of Scope for Phase 1: Real-time notification delivery Email/SMS integration Notification queue processing 1. 3 Key Features 1. 3. 1 Event Classification The system categorizes events into multiple classifications: REALTIME: Events requiring immediate notification NON_REALTIME: Events stored for historical reference without notifications CRITICAL/ERROR: High-priority events with immediate alerting INFO/WARNING: Informational events for monitoring STARTUP_EVENT/SHUTDOWN_EVENT: System lifecycle events 1. 3. 2 Flexible Event Data Storage Events utilize a hybrid storage approach: Structured fields for common attributes (date, time, user, program, etc. ) JSON-based DBEVT_DATA field for event-specific information Supports unlimited custom fields without schema changes 1. 3. 3 Multi-Language Support The system supports bilingual descriptions and messages: English (_E suffix) and French (_F suffix) variants for all descriptive fields Configurable message templates for different locales 1. 3.

Rather than building a complex system upfront, we began with basic event logging and gradually added sophistication based on real-world needs. 2. 2 The Core Design – Understanding the Foundation Before diving into how we got here, let's look at the current core design that evolved from our iterations: 2. 2. 1 The Six-Table Architecture EVENT_TRACKING (Main Event Storage) v [Links via DBEVT_CONFIG_ID] EVENT_TRACKING_CONFIG_DETAIL (Program Configuration) v [Links via category_id and type_id] EVENT_LOG_CATEGORY & EVENT_LOG_TYPE (Reference Data) v [All joined in] USER_EVENT_TRACKING (User Subscriptions) v [Filtered by user subscriptions] EVENT_TRACKING_KICK (Notification Signal) v [Links via event_id to EVENT_TRACKING] USER_EVENTS_VIEW (Unified View) Note: Our system is built on six interconnected tables that work together. 2. 3 Evolution Stage 1: The Beginning 2. 3. 1 Initial Challenge We need to track what's happening in our systems. 2. 3.

This led to our first major refactoring: EVENT_TRACKING_CATEGORY { DBEVT_CATEGORY_ID -- Now using IDs! DBEVT_CATEGORY_NAME -- 'REPORT', 'SAMPLE', 'SCALE' DBEVT_CATEGORY_DESC_F/E -- Bilingual support added } EVENT_TRACKING_TYPE { DBEVT_TYPE_ID DBEVT_TYPE_NAME -- 'AUDITRP', 'SAMPLE', 'TSGUI' DBEVT_TYPE_DESC_F/E } But we still had a problem: How do we link events to these references without changing existing applications? 2. 5 Evolution Stage 3: The Configuration Layer 2. 5. 1 The Breakthrough – Configuration Table This is when we introduced EVENT_TRACKING_CONFIG_DETAIL: EVENT_TRACKING_CONFIG_DETAIL { dbevt_config_id -- Unique config identifier dbevt_program -- Which program? dbevt_category_id -- Links to EVENT_LOG_CATEGORY dbevt_type_id -- Links to EVENT_LOG_TYPE dbevt_event_classification -- REALTIME, NON_REALTIME, etc. } 2. 5. 2 The Clever Connection Instead of changing EVENT_TRACKING structure dramatically, we: Added just one field: DBEVT_CONFIG_ID Applications pass config_id instead of category/type The config table handles all the mappings EVENT_TRACKING { ... EVENT_TRACKING (Main Transaction Table) Purpose: Stores individual event occurrences with minimal data by referencing configuration details through config_id. This is the primary transactional table that records each event execution. Design Philosophy: Keep the transaction table lean by storing only event-specific runtime data. Static configuration data is referenced via foreign key to avoid redundancy. Fields Description: Field Name Data Type Constraint Description DBEVT_UNIQUE_ID INT PRIMARY KEY Unique identifier for each event record. Auto-incremented sequence number that uniquely identifies every event logged in the system. DBEVT_DATE DATE NOT NULL The date when the event occurred (YYYY-MM-DD). Used for temporal querying, reporting, and event chronology. Essential for audit trails and compliance. DBEVT_TIME TIME NOT NULL The time when the event occurred (HH:MM:SS). Provides precise timing information for the event. Combined with DBEVT_DATE gives complete timestamp.

This is the key field that enables data normalization - links to all static configuration information about the program/event type. 2. 8. 2. EVENT_TRACKING_CONFIG_DETAIL (Configuration Master Table) Purpose: Stores reusable program configurations. Acts as a master reference table that contains all static information about programs, their classifications, and logging settings. Each unique program configuration gets one record. Design Philosophy: Centralize all program metadata in one place. When the same program executes multiple times, EVENT_TRACKING only stores the config_id reference, not the full program details. Links this configuration to a predefined category (e. g. , "Batch Process", "User Interface", "API Call"). DBEVT_TYPE_ID INT FOREIGN KEY Reference to EVENT_TRACKING_TYPE table. Links this configuration to a predefined type (e. g. , "Start", "End", "Error", "Warning"). DBEVT_DESC_E VARCHAR(64) Event description in English. Used in notification messages and UI display. EVENT_TRACKING_KICK (Notification Signal Table) Purpose: Stores lightweight signal records that notify the background Notification Service when new events require notification processing. Each record links to a specific event in EVENT_TRACKING and tracks whether the service has processed it. Design Philosophy: Keep event insertion fast by separating the notification signal from notification processing. The DLL inserts a minimal kick record immediately after logging an event, then signals the service via IPC. The service processes kick records asynchronously, avoiding any performance impact on the calling application. DBETK_STATUS CHAR(1) DEFAULT 'P' Processing status. 'P' = Pending (awaiting service), 'C' = Complete (processed), 'F' = Failed (error occurred).

DBETK_PROCESSED_DT DATETIME NULL Timestamp when the Notification Service finished processing this record. NULL until processed. DBETK_PRIORITY INT DEFAULT 5 Processing priority set by the DLL based on event classification from EVENT_TRACKING_CONFIG_DETAIL at insert time. Lower values are processed first by the Notification Service. Values: 1=REALTIME, 2=CRITICAL, 3=ERROR, 4=WARNING, 5=INFO, 6=NON_REALTIME, 7=STARTUP_EVENT, 8=SHUTDOWN_EVENT. New priority levels can be added without changes to the Notification Service. Business Rules: One kick record is created per event insert when logging is enabled, regardless of classification. The Notification Service uses the DBETK_PRIORITY to prioritize processing order. The DLL inserts the kick record immediately after the EVENT_TRACKING insert succeeds The Notification Service updates status from 'P' to 'C' or 'F' after processing Completed kick records can be periodically purged for housekeeping If the service is down, kick records accumulate with status 'P' and are processed when the service restarts CHAPTER 3 – HOW WE STORE THE DATA Our event tracking system uses a normalized database design with a configuration-based reference system. The key innovation is separating static program configuration from dynamic event data, combined with centralized logging control through a DLL interface. User subscriptions allow individual users to define which events they want to see and be notified about. The Core Concept: Three reference tables are pre-populated with master data: EVENT_TRACKING_CATEGORY: Defines event categories (e. g. , "REPORT", "SCALE") EVENT_TRACKING_TYPE: Defines event types (e. g. , "ADUITRP") EVENT_TRACKING_CONFIG_DETAIL: Contains unique program configurations Each program configuration is identified by a unique combination of program name and parameters, which maps to a single config_id. This config_id also stores a critical dbevt_logging_enabled flag ('Y' or 'N').

A fourth table, USER_EVENT_TRACKING, stores per-user subscriptions linking users to specific event configurations with notification preferences and optional filter criteria. A fifth table, EVENT_TRACKING_KICK, stores lightweight signal records that link to EVENT_TRACKING and notify the background Notification Service when new events need notification processing. How It Works: Step 1: Program Initialization When a program starts, it calls a DLL function which: Automatically identifies the computer and calling program name Captures the command-line parameters Looks up the matching record in EVENT_TRACKING_CONFIG_DETAIL Returns: config_id (unique identifier for this program configuration) logging_enabled flag ('Y' or 'N') Step 2: Event Logging Decision Throughout program execution, when events occur: The program checks the logging_enabled flag If 'Y': Proceed to log the event If 'N': Skip logging entirely (no database operation) Step 3: Event Recording When logging is enabled, the program: Collects event-specific details (date, time, user, sequence, data) Calls another DLL function to insert the event record Stores only: Runtime event data The config_id reference (not the full program details) After a successful insert, the DLL: Inserts a kick record into EVENT_TRACKING_KICK with the event_id, priority (mapped from event classification), and status 'P' Signals the Notification Service via IPC (Named Event) to process the new kick record The calling application returns immediately — notification processing happens asynchronously in the background service Every event gets a kick record. The DLL maps the event classification to a priority value in the kick record. The Notification Service processes kick records in priority order (lower values first), ensuring REALTIME and CRITICAL events are handled before INFO or NON_REALTIME events.
